datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: The entire dataset is constructed from English source data. Basic Questions were first created in English, then translated to 22 other languages.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: After completing the English version data expansion, we translated the data into 22 other languages.

details.notes: The benchmark tests instruction-following mechanics (format, keywords, length, repetition, punctuation, citation, emoji, style, tone, content, language_switch) rather than culturally-grounded knowledge. While translations were checked for naturalness and language-specific features (e.g., Bengali numerals, CJK full-width punctuation), the tasks themselves are not culturally grounded.

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: All personnel we hired for instruction data translation and dataset quality control were native speakers of their respective languages, and they possessed near-native English proficiency. We invited native speakers to review instructions in each language, ensuring expressions adhered to language conventions.

annotator_workforce.compensation_details: The translations were carried out by internal research team members as part of their responsibilities, thus no additional compensation was involved.
annotator_workforce.evidence: The total number of questionnaire participants was 31 people, of which 19 were male, 12 were female, most people's age distribution was 21-39 years old, and all respondents had high-frequency usage habits of LLMs.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The benchmark is entirely English-centric in construction: all Basic Questions and Instructions were created in English first and then translated. The evaluation framework extends IFEval (an English-only benchmark) to 23 languages. While language-specific evaluation rules were developed (e.g., for word counting, keyword matching, punctuation), the underlying task design and content originate from English.

notably_excluded: Most of Africa beyond Zulu and Malagasy
Indigenous languages of North America and Australia
geographic_representation.evidence: MaXIFE covers 23 languages spanning Indo-European (8), Austronesian (4), Dravidian (2), Turkic (2), Sino-Tibetan (1), Japonic (1), Koreanic (1), Kartvelian (1), Niger-Congo (1), and Quechuan (1) families.
